item.text:
{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q024_fibronectin_fragment_selection","answer":"Treat d1o5dt2 as incomplete evidence for an established family member. In SCOPe 2.08, d1o5dt2 (SUNID 103884; 1o5d T:107–205), from human tissue factor, carries the domain-level annotation “fr”: missing more than one-third of the common structure and/or sequence. d1uc6a1 (SUNID 107766; 1uc6 A:6–109), from human ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor alpha, has no corresponding fragment flag in the retrieved annotations.

For alignment, align the homologous sequence and structural core actually represented in both domains. Mark unavailable regions as missing data rather than interpreting them as evolutionary deletions or forcing a full-domain correspondence. Report aligned length and coverage alongside sequence identity or structural similarity: a good match over a fragment does not demonstrate agreement across the complete domain. The nominal residue ranges alone do not establish structural completeness; inspect observed coordinates, deposited sequence and full-length sequence to establish what is absent.

For a general family representative or full-domain modeling template, prefer a verified complete, well-resolved member. Between these two, d1uc6a1 is the better initial candidate on completeness grounds, but absence of a fragment flag does not establish its quality or make it optimal for every target. Check coverage, experimental quality and target relevance. Retain d1o5dt2 for tissue-factor-specific comparisons or local templates where its observed region is useful; it cannot directly template missing regions.

The fragment annotation does not revoke membership in family b.1.2.1 (SUNID 49266). Both also belong to superfamily b.1.2, fold b.1 (immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich), and class b (all beta proteins). Family membership supports close evolutionary relatedness; superfamily membership supports broader common ancestry, whereas fold or class alone does not establish homology. Count d1o5dt2 as family evidence, but do not treat incompleteness as a distinct architecture, natural truncation or extra evolutionary diversity. Compare diversity over shared coverage and account for redundant sampling. Their different parent proteins illustrate biological breadth; neither shared family membership nor fragment similarity justifies transferring tissue-factor activity, receptor specificity or binding-site function without independent functional evidence.","evidence_used":["Pretrained model knowledge","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/annotations"]}]}
